C has a constant-depth F4 sum-of-products-of-homogeneous-linear-forms formula of size O_Delta(s^3). Use C=omega^2 D+omega sigma(D) for the earlier F4 certificate, with coefficientwise Frobenius fixing letters. No constant-depth F2 formula or membership in the matched shallow simulation image is claimed.

claim.summary: For fixed maximum degree Delta, canonical positive integer-flow CNFs on a nonempty finite simple graph with n vertices and m edges have original-input noncommutative IPS formulas of size O_Delta((n+m+1)^4) and constant ordered unbounded-fan-in depth over K=F_(2^a) of size O(m+1), retaining Boolean and commutator generators. A binary-coefficient certificate has a constant-depth K formula with an extra O(log(m+2)) size factor, by coefficientwise trace. Local Laurent characters cancel globally while positivity removes the constant coefficient; interpolate exponents [-2m,2m] at 4m+1 nonzero points. Isolated vertices have a unit input. No binary constant-depth formula or simultaneous small word-rank claim for flow is made.
claim.assessment: Working complete Laurent-parameter and field-trace construction, passed by the sole fresh GPT-6.1-Sol medium reviewer with exact local GAP controls. Shallow extension formulas need not have small word flattenings; binary constant-depth complexity remains open.

claim.summary: There is no generic polynomial-size fixed-depth operation extracting arbitrary homogeneous components from all polynomial-size fixed-depth binary arithmetic circuits of polynomial degree. Already G_n=product(1+x_i), q=2^a, n=2q-1 has degree-q component e_q evaluating to majority, since binomial(w,q) mod2 is the a-th bit of w. Such an operation would contradict Smolensky's majority lower bound for AC0[2]. Binary constants and unbounded-fanin gates with wire size are essential.
claim.assessment: Working attributed elementary consequence of the published majority lower bound, medium reviewed. Does not rule out special component extraction with additional hypotheses or large-field interpolation.

claim.summary: Canonical forbidden-assignment CNF encodings of positive integer-flow constraints on graphs, with polynomial encoding length in m Boolean edge variables, have PC refutation degree <=m/2-Omega(m/log m). They cannot meet the moving old-degree hypothesis at approximation depth ell>=3. Fixed maximum degree also excludes the depth2 window; growing-degree depth2 and noncanonical encodings are not settled.
claim.assessment: Working corollary over every field after Boolean predicate encoding. Net flows sum to zero, so constraints are unsatisfiable; at least half local assignments are forbidden, forcing Delta=O(log m) under polynomial canonical encoding length. The bound includes both the frontier cost and the original local conversion reserve. No Frege proof-size conclusion follows.
